title.tl: Pagtatagumpay ng Kamatayan sa Paglipas ng Buhay

description.en:
Obscurantism kills enlightenment, is the message of “Triumph of Death Over Life”. The hooded skeletal figure is the Spanish colonial government, the corpse of a woman still in her youth, represents the Philippines. Rizal believed that Spain obstructed enlightenment and liberalism thus killing the country’s aspirations for political and economic progress.

In 1890, when Rizal was in Belgium, he sent Scientia and Triumph of Death Over Life to his friend, Austrian Professor Ferdinand Blumentritt, as “little tokens of remembrance.”

Blumentritt sent his gratitude and admiration in a letter to Rizal on 29 September 1890: “The statuette Triumph of Death over Life” has been admired by two German artists… of opposite viewpoints, the Berliner being a cold realist and the Viennese who is really from Leitmeritz and a Slav, an idealist of sensitive feelings - admire your statuettes. They are both agreed in the sublimity of the conception and execution of the statuette representing the triumph of death over life”.

A sculptural reproduction was made by Anastacio Caedo based on the replica previously made by Guillermo Tolentino in 1961. Currently, it is exhibited in Gallery 5 (Ang Unang Paglalakbay ni Rizal sa Europa, 1882-1887) of the Museo ni Jose Rizal in Calamba, Laguna.

description.fil:
Pinapaslang ng obskurantismo ang kaliwanagan — ito ang mensahe ng “Triumph of Death Over Life.” Ang nakatalukbong na pigurang tila kalansay ay ang pamahalaang kolonyal na Espanyol, at ang bangkay ng babaeng nasa kabataan pa ay kumakatawan sa Pilipinas. Naniniwala si Rizal na hinarangan ng Espanya ang kaliwanagan at liberalismo at sa gayon ay pinatay ang mga hangarin ng bansa tungo sa pag-unlad na pampulitika at pang-ekonomiya.

Noong 1890, nang nasa Belgium si Rizal, ipinadala niya ang Scientia at ang Triumph of Death Over Life sa kanyang kaibigan, ang propesor Austriyakong si Ferdinand Blumentritt, bilang “maliliit na alaala.”

Ipinarating ni Blumentritt ang kanyang pasasalamat at paghanga sa isang liham kay Rizal noong 29 Setyembre 1890: “Ang estatwilyang Triumph of Death over Life ay hinangaan ng dalawang Alemang alagad ng sining… na may magkasalungat na pananaw, ang taga-Berlin na isang malamig na realista at ang taga-Vienna na talagang mula sa Leitmeritz at isang Slav, isang idealistang may madamdaming damdamin — hinahangaan nila ang inyong mga estatwilya. Pareho silang nagkakasundo sa kadakilaan ng pagkakaisip at pagkakagawa ng estatwilyang kumakatawan sa pagtatagumpay ng kamatayan sa buhay.”

Isang reproduksiyong eskultural ang ginawa ni Anastacio Caedo batay sa replikang dating ginawa ni Guillermo Tolentino noong 1961. Sa kasalukuyan, nakatanghal ito sa Gallery 5 (Ang Unang Paglalakbay ni Rizal sa Europa, 1882–1887) ng Museo ni Jose Rizal sa Calamba, Laguna.

description.de:
Obskurantismus tötet die Aufklärung – das ist die Botschaft von „Triumph of Death Over Life“. Die vermummte Skelettgestalt ist die spanische Kolonialregierung, der Leichnam einer noch jungen Frau steht für die Philippinen. Rizal war überzeugt, Spanien behindere Aufklärung und Liberalismus und ersticke damit die Hoffnungen des Landes auf politischen und wirtschaftlichen Fortschritt.

1890, während seines Aufenthalts in Belgien, sandte Rizal Scientia und Triumph of Death Over Life an seinen Freund, den österreichischen Professor Ferdinand Blumentritt, als „kleine Andenken“.

Blumentritt sprach ihm seinen Dank und seine Bewunderung in einem Brief vom 29. September 1890 aus: „Die Statuette Triumph of Death over Life ist von zwei deutschen Künstlern bewundert worden… von entgegengesetzter Richtung – der Berliner ein kühler Realist, der Wiener, der eigentlich aus Leitmeritz stammt und ein Slawe ist, ein Idealist von feinem Empfinden – beide bewundern Ihre Statuetten. Beide stimmen überein in der Erhabenheit der Auffassung und der Ausführung jener Statuette, die den Triumph des Todes über das Leben darstellt.“

Eine bildhauerische Nachbildung schuf Anastacio Caedo nach der Replik, die Guillermo Tolentino 1961 angefertigt hatte. Sie ist derzeit in Galerie 5 (Ang Unang Paglalakbay ni Rizal sa Europa, 1882–1887) des Museo ni Jose Rizal in Calamba, Laguna, ausgestellt.
